value: This collection of reviews discusses René Descartes' seminal philosophical treatise, "Meditations on First Philosophy," highlighting its systematic application of doubt to establish foundational truths. The work, structured as a series of meditations followed by objections and responses, is recognized for establishing the certainty of the thinking self ("cogito ergo sum"), arguing for the existence of God and the external world through "clear and distinct ideas," and introducing mind-body dualism. Reviewers consistently acknowledge its monumental importance as a cornerstone of modern Western philosophy, despite frequently debating the logical coherence of its arguments, particularly the perceived circularity in the proofs for God's existence. The "Meditations" remains influential, stimulating profound philosophical inquiry.
